content:
maya.chen: Quick share — ran a fast sweep comparing PCIe vs SXM intra-node configs for a 30B LLM (int8 quant) across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Variables: NVLink enabled/disabled, NUMA pinning on/off, kernel selection flags. High-level: SXM+NVLink+NUMA pin gave ~2.1x sustained throughput vs a PCIe node and ~30% better p95 latency. Charts: https://redwood.internal/pres/bench/1751234567.png

liam.k: Nice. Can you paste the raw numbers? batch sizes / seq len?

maya.chen: Pasted CSV below and the exact command. seq_len=1024, batch=4 (client-level), tokens/sec measured at tail-stable window.

```
config,region,gpus,link,numa,p95_latency_ms,tokens_per_sec
SXM_NVLink_PIN,us-west-2,4,SXM+NVLink, pinned, 42, 12100
SXM_NVLink_NOPIN,us-west-2,4,SXM+NVLink, unpinned, 58, 9800
SXM_NOPLUG_PIN,us-west-2,4,SXM(no-NV), pinned, 65, 8300
PCIE_PIN,us-west-2,4,PCIe, pinned, 95, 5800
PCIE_NOPIN,us-west-2,4,PCIe, unpinned, 110, 5100
SXM_NVLink_PIN,eu-west-1,4,SXM+NVLink, pinned, 48, 10900
PCIE_PIN,eu-west-1,4,PCIe, pinned, 102, 5600
```

jordan: Those are solid deltas. Was model sharded across devices (tensor parallel) or replicated with pipeline?

maya.chen: TP=1, model-parallel via sharded weights (1D TP), KV cache kept local; inference runtime used continuous batching. No pipeline parallelism for these runs.

nina: Did you toggle any of the kernel flags? like `use_cuda_graphs`, `fused_attention`, or the `prefer_fp16_gemm` path?

maya.chen: Yes — default runtime picks `flash_attn_v2` on SXM builds, fallback to `flash_attn_v1` on PCIe GPUs due to kernel availability. I also tested `--force-fused-gemm=false` briefly and saw ~5% drop in throughput on SXM. `use_cuda_graphs=true` reduced jitter in p95 by ~8% but didn't change median.

rachel: Node types? A100 80GB SXM4 vs A100 40GB PCIe? or v5?

sre-bot: Node inventory: SXM nodes = a100-80gb-sxm4 (nvlink topo all-to-all), PCIe nodes = a100-40gb-pcie (no nvlink), both Ubuntu 22.04, driver 535.86, cuda 12.2, MPS disabled.

liam.k: Interesting that NUMA pinning matters even with NVLink. Any hypothesis?

maya.chen: Hypothesis: NVLink helps inter-GPU tensor comms for KV/cache and attention matmuls, but NUMA pinning reduces CPU-GPU PCIe hops for control/IO + reduces cross-socket memory placements for the host process. On PCIe nodes, if host process threads bounce across sockets you get extra PCIe hops => latency tail. On SXM the inter-gpu paths are fast so NUMA pinning still helps but less dramatically.

perf-bot: Perf summary (auto): SXM_NVLink_PIN shows best cost-performance for steady-state inference at target SLO p95<=50ms. Recommend scaling factor 2.0x capacity for PCIe-to-SXM migration planning.

jordan: Did you try different batch sizes? scaling behavior matters for autoscaler rules.

maya.chen: Yes, quick sweep: batch=1,2,4,8. SXM scales near-linearly up to 8; PCIe saturates earlier. Rough tokens/sec for SXM_NVLink_PIN: {1:3200,2:6400,4:12100,8:16200}. PCIe_PIN: {1:1500,2:3000,4:5800,8:7600}. I'll add these to the dashboard.

nina: Any quality impact from the quantization? int8 was done with outlier clipping + K-scaling?

maya.chen: Quant pipeline was per-channel symmetric int8 with KL calibration on a 5k prompt set. No observable ROUGE/EM regressions >0.3% vs fp16 baseline on our eval set. We'll keep a guarded rollout.

rachel: Action items?

maya.chen: 1) Jordan/rachel: update autoscaler rules for regions with PCIe nodes to assume ~0.5x token/s vs SXM. 2) Eng-runtime: add flag to prefer `flash_attn_v2` fallback into PCIe build if kernel compiles. 3) Bench team: schedule 24h run to check thermal throttling on SXM under 99th pct load. I'll file tickets.

liam.k: Can you attach the run scripts and the experiment note? I want to reproduce on a 70B config.

maya.chen: Uploaded run script + note to /mnt/bench/1751234567/ and linked in the perf dashboard. Ping me if can't access. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Note: follow-up benchmark scheduled for 1751310000 (24h run) — will post results in this thread.
